truths.CP2:
WITH one_variant AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(variant) AS variant, MIN(assigned_at) AS assigned_at
  FROM ab_assignments
  WHERE test_id = 'AB-2025-01'
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id)
FROM one_variant o
JOIN ab_conversions c ON c.test_id = 'AB-2025-01' AND c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND c.converted_at >= o.assigned_at
WHERE o.variant = 'control'
truths.CP4:
WITH one_variant AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(variant) AS variant, MIN(assigned_at) AS assigned_at
  FROM ab_assignments
  WHERE test_id = 'AB-2025-01'
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
),
rates AS (
  SELECT o.variant, 1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS rate
  FROM one_variant o
  LEFT JOIN ab_conversions c ON c.test_id = 'AB-2025-01' AND c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND c.converted_at >= o.assigned_at
  GROUP BY o.variant
)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (t.rate - k.rate) / k.rate, 1)
FROM rates k
JOIN rates t ON k.variant = 'control' AND t.variant = 'treatment'

CP5.explanation: The interval of the difference runs from below zero to about one point, so the test cannot yet tell a small gain from no effect; a clean split makes the test trustworthy, but it does not make the gain real.
